governingStandard.why: Well-formedness is not decoration here; it is the discriminator. G23 exists to prove that a payload the host cannot fault at the type layer is still refused at the content layer — relation-registry refusal before fact admission, and domain-mutation refusal with sufficiency host-owned. A fixture that is ill-typed is refused earlier and for a different reason, and the record it produces proves nothing about the property under test. Findings M1, M4 and M5 all reduce to this: the authored bytes are hostile-and-malformed where hostile-but-well-formed was named.
governingStandard.whatTheCorpusGotRight: Field sets are exact. The NT-3 fixture carries precisely the 14 required FactCandidateV1 fields; both Coverage payloads carry precisely the 4 required CoverageV1 fields, 5 required CoverageResultV1 fields per entry, and 8 required CoverageKeyV1 fields per key, with no unknown members anywhere. relation/resolution/layer are correct against live relationRegistry (declares → layer syntax, ladder [syntactic]; file → [enumerated]; package → [manifest-declared]). The artifact's authorityClaim is literally accurate that it 'quotes closed FactCandidateV1 and CoverageV1 field names'. The defects are in field values, in the invented baseline encoding, and in ordering — not in the field names.

findings.title: Sha256Text form is violated at 17 sites across all three fixtures, so none of them is well-formed
findings.live: delivery.v2 wireSchema.definitions.Sha256Text = 'text matching ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'. definitions.TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey = 'Sha256Text = SHA-256(UTF8(\'opensip.typescript-universe.v1\') || 0x00 || CVE1(TypeScriptSemanticUniverseV1))'. CoverageKeyV1.sourceUniverseId and .targetUniverseId are TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey / canonical universe identity; CoverageKeyV1.subjectScopeCommitment is 'Sha256Text commitment to the exact examined subject set'; CoverageV1.coverageCommitment is 'Sha256Text over deterministic-CBOR entries'. fact-plane candidateSchema.sourceUniverseId = 'canonical sha256:<64 lowercase hex> and exact admitted source universe'. Live worked examples agree without exception: delivery.v2 coverageDomain.vectors[0] keys carry 'sha256:aaaa…' and 'sha256:a78e6a72…'; fact-plane vectors[0].candidate carries sourceUniverseId 'sha256:1111…', targetUniverseId 'sha256:1111…' and anchors[0].snapshotId 'snap1:sha256:85e066e5…'.
findings.authored: Every one of these fields carries a bare 64-hex string with no 'sha256:' prefix. NT-3: sourceUniverseId, targetUniverseId, anchors[0].snapshotId (3 sites — and snapshotId additionally omits the live 'snap1:' snapshot-namespace prefix). declares-complete: key.sourceUniverseId, key.targetUniverseId, key.subjectScopeCommitment, coverageCommitment (4 sites). widens: the same three key fields on each of three keys, plus coverageCommitment (10 sites). Total 17.
findings.whyItMatters: This is a type-layer defect, not a fixture-local substitution. The corpus is entitled to substitute fixture-local VALUES for live Run identity — whatIsNotAuthored says so and fixtureLocalPins.standing labels them FIXTURE-LOCAL, which I accept. It is not entitled to substitute a different FORM. A host validating these payloads rejects sourceUniverseId as not matching ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ before it ever consults the relation registry or compares the coverage domain.
findings.failureScenario: G23 executes the NT-3 member. The host refuses the candidate for a malformed sourceUniverseId. The retained record shows 'no fact admitted, no Finding produced' — which is exactly what the NT-3 pass words demand — and the member scores PASS having never exercised the host-owned relation registry at all. The identical masquerade with a well-formed sourceUniverseId would still be untested. The same holds for both NT-5 members, whose keys are refused on subjectScopeCommitment form before any domain comparison occurs.
findings.remedy: Prefix all 17 values with 'sha256:' and give the NT-3 anchor snapshotId the live 'snap1:sha256:' form, keeping the fixture-local digests. Note this changes all three fixture digests and therefore every digest cited in authoredCatalog and recordedInputs.

findings.title: coverageCommitment is a SHA-256 over compact JSON, not over deterministic-CBOR, and no construction is declared for it
findings.recomputation: Both reproduce exactly as SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON serialization of the entries array in file insertion order — Python json.dumps(entries, separators=(',',':')). Preimage lengths 524 and 1574 bytes; both digests matched on the first attempt. The preimage is JSON text beginning [{"stageId":"fixture.g23.stage","entryOrdinal":0,… — not deterministic-CBOR, which would begin with an array header byte and would sort each key map by encoded-key bytes rather than preserving authored order.
findings.whyItMatters: Three compounding problems. First, the preimage is the wrong encoding for the field the closed type defines. Second, the construction is declared nowhere: fixtureLocalPins names four constructions and this is not among them, even though it is the fourth synthesized value in the authored bytes. I verified the other three reproduce exactly from their stated preimages, which makes the omission conspicuous rather than incidental — a reviewer checking only what the artifact declares would never look at this field. Third, whatIsNotAuthored[5] disclaims 'CVE1/deterministic-CBOR coverageCommitment verification' and fixtureLocalPins.standing repeats 'Not CVE1/deterministic-CBOR coverageCommitment verification' — but the bytes do not carry that disclaimer, and a 64-hex value sitting at a field defined as 'Sha256Text over deterministic-CBOR entries' reads as exactly the thing being disclaimed. A disclaimer in the catalog does not travel with the fixture into the harness.
findings.failureScenario: A later execution cycle recomputes coverageCommitment per the closed type, gets a different digest than the one in the fixture bytes, and refuses the payload as a commitment mismatch — again pre-empting the domain-mutation refusal the member exists to observe. Or worse: a reader takes the pinned value as a verified CVE1 commitment because nothing in the fixture says otherwise.
findings.remedy: Either compute both commitments over deterministic-CBOR entries per RFC 8949 restricted profile and pin them in Sha256Text form, or add an explicit fixtureLocalPins.coverageCommitment entry stating the fixture-local construction verbatim and the fact that it is not the closed-type preimage. The first is preferable; the second is the minimum honest floor.

findings.title: hostRequestedDomainBaseline invents a Coverage-domain encoding vocabulary and under-determines the requested domain
findings.live: The requested domain has exactly one live encoding: delivery.v2 definitions.RequestedCoverageDomainV1, closed, required [subjectScope, keys, domainCommitment], where keys is a 'non-empty sorted unique array of full CoverageKeyV1' and domainCommitment is 'Sha256Text = SHA-256(UTF8(\'opensip.ts-provider.requested-coverage-domain.v1\') || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR({subjectScope,keys}))'. coverageDomain.keyConstruction fixes all eight key fields and orders them by 'ascending deterministic-CBOR bytes'. coverageDomain.closed is true. coverageDomain.vectors[0] shows the shape worked end to end.
findings.authored: Three-element and two-element arrays of slash-joined strings: ['declares/syntactic','file/enumerated'] on the narrows and widens members, and ['declares/syntactic recorded unknown'] on the unknown-to-covered member.
findings.verification: grep for 'declares/syntactic', 'file/enumerated' and 'package/manifest-declared' across delivery.v2.json, fact-plane.v1.json, the live occupancy v2 and g23-input-corpus.v1 returns zero hits. The slash shorthand originates in this artifact.
findings.whyItMatters: whatIsAuthored makes this field load-bearing: 'Host-requested domain baselines live in this catalog, not as extra closed-type fields on the payloads.' That placement decision is sound — adding fields to a closed payload would be worse. But having made the catalog the baseline, the catalog must author it to exact bytes, and a relation/rung shorthand cannot. It supplies 2 of the 8 CoverageKeyV1 fields, no subjectScope, no domainCommitment, and no deterministic-CBOR ordering. Narrowing, widening and unknown-to-covered are all defined as differences against the full key set in key order, so a baseline that cannot express a full key in order cannot define the mutation under test. And 'declares/syntactic recorded unknown' additionally smuggles a live coverageState enum word into the key slot of a field whose other members hold keys alone, so the field's own element vocabulary is inconsistent between members.
findings.contradictsItsOwnClaim: authorityClaim asserts 'It does not invent a Coverage-domain encoding vocabulary' and doesNot[4] repeats 'Does not invent a Coverage-domain encoding vocabulary.' Both are falsified by this field. Live occupancy v2 retainedEvidence[2].exactByteIntent independently forbids it: 'This member … does not invent a Coverage-domain encoding.'
findings.remedy: Author each baseline as a full RequestedCoverageDomainV1 — subjectScope, sorted full CoverageKeyV1 array, domainCommitment — either as a fourth authored fixture file or as an explicitly fixture-local block in the catalog, with the unknown baseline expressed as a key plus coverageState 'unknown' rather than as prose.

findings.title: file and package are not typescript-semantic coverage relations, so both NT-5 baselines are unconstructible for this provider
findings.live: delivery.v2 coverageDomain.relationResolutionById (inside coverageDomain, closed: true) = {declares: syntactic, imports: resolved-target, references: resolved-binding, calls: resolved-callee, types: checked, reachability: from-resolved-calls}. Neither file nor package appears. coverageDomain.keyConstruction.resolution = 'relationResolutionById[relation]'. coverageDomain.relationSource = 'the exact typescript-semantic relation/rung map in the selected signed install-profile capability manifest; a stage relation outside this map is denied by bundled-semantic-provider-stage'.
findings.authored: The narrows and widens baselines both include file/enumerated as a host-requested key. The widens payload adds package/manifest-declared as the unrequested key. The catalog justifies the latter as 'an unrequested live relationRegistry key'.
findings.whyItMatters: The justification cites the wrong registry. fact-plane relationRegistry is the global relation registry — file and package are genuinely live there, with layer inventory and the exact rungs used, which is why this is easy to miss. But a TypeScript-provider Coverage key is constructed from the provider-scoped coverageDomain map, and a stage relation outside that map is denied at stage admission. Consequences differ per member and both are fatal. For narrows: the baseline it narrows FROM is not a domain the host can request of this provider, so the member's premise does not exist. For widens: the added key would be denied as an out-of-map stage relation rather than refused as a domain widening.
findings.failureScenario: The widens member is executed. The stage is denied by bundled-semantic-provider-stage because package is outside the typescript-semantic relation/rung map. No Coverage frame is ever evaluated, so the host never demonstrates that it refuses a widened domain — yet the record shows a refusal and the member reads as PASS.
findings.remedy: Draw every baseline and every added key from relationResolutionById. A widening key must be an in-map relation the stage did not request — for example types/checked or references/resolved-binding — and the narrows baseline must be two in-map keys, so that the only fault is the domain difference.

findings.title: widens entries are not in deterministic-CBOR key order, so the widening cannot be attributed
findings.where: G23.nt5.coverage-widens.json entries, and authoredCatalog baseline ordering
findings.live: delivery.v2 CoverageV1.entries = 'non-empty ordered array containing exactly one CoverageResultV1 per full key in this stage's requestedCoverageDomain.keys, in key order'. RequestedCoverageDomainV1.keys = 'non-empty sorted unique array of full CoverageKeyV1'. coverageDomain.keyConstruction.ordering = 'sort full CoverageKeyV1 maps by ascending deterministic-CBOR bytes and reject duplicates'. coverageDomain.validation = 'A missing, duplicate, unordered, altered or unrequested key is provider-protocol / PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; no partial domain is admitted.'
findings.recomputation: I encoded the three authored keys as deterministic-CBOR text-keyed maps (RFC 8949 restricted profile, keys sorted by encoded-key bytes, matching fact-plane canonicalPayloadEncoding.mapOrder) and sorted the resulting maps bytewise. All three maps share an identical prefix through the producer entry, so the sort is decided at the relation value: 0x64'file' < 0x67'package' < 0x68'declares'. Canonical order is therefore file/enumerated, package/manifest-declared, declares/syntactic. The authored order is declares/syntactic (entryOrdinal 0), file/enumerated (1), package/manifest-declared (2) — the canonical order reversed at the head. The catalog baselines are also non-canonical: ['declares/syntactic','file/enumerated'] sorts to ['file/enumerated','declares/syntactic'].
findings.whyItMatters: Unordered and unrequested keys carry the identical refusal token, PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The widens fixture therefore carries two hostile properties that are indistinguishable in the retained record, and the member cannot prove that the host refused the WIDENING as opposed to the ordering. This is the same attribution failure as M1 and M4, arriving by a third independent route, which is itself the signal: the corpus was authored against field lists rather than against the ordering and construction rules that sit beside them.
findings.remedy: Emit entries in ascending deterministic-CBOR key order with entryOrdinal contiguous from 0 in that order, and list every catalog baseline in the same canonical order, so ordering is never a second fault.

findings.title: NT-3 stores a hex transcription under the wire field name canonicalRelationPayload
findings.live: fact-plane candidateSchema.transportRepresentation: 'canonicalRelationPayload is a deterministic-CBOR byte string. JSON vectors transcribe those bytes as canonicalRelationPayloadHex; that transcription is not an additional wire field.' The live vector fact-id-v1-typescript-declares does exactly that: it carries canonicalRelationPayloadHex plus a companion decodedRelationPayload, and no canonicalRelationPayload field at all.
findings.authored: The hex text 'a0' under the wire name canonicalRelationPayload, with no decodedRelationPayload companion.
findings.whyItMatters: For an artifact whose stated purpose is 'independently pinning exact-byte implementations', this is precisely the ambiguity that must not survive: a loader cannot tell whether the field holds two characters of text or the single CBOR byte 0xa0. The corpus knows the distinction — its own pin is named fixtureLocalPins.canonicalRelationPayloadHex — but the authored bytes use the other name, so the artifact and its fixture disagree.
findings.relatedObservation: The 'a0' empty map does not conform to opensip.relation.declares.v1, which requires container, declared and declarationKind. I do NOT raise that as a separate defect: occupancy v2 NT-3 exactByteIntent says 'whose relationSchemaId or payload is provider-minted or mismatched', so a mismatched payload is within the named intent, and the corpus labels it the 'NT-3 mismatch limb'. It is worth noting only that the live negative fixture for this exact case — fact-plane negativeFixtures 'reject-unknown-relation-schema', expected FACT_RELATION_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN — mutates relationSchemaId alone as a delta on the base vector and keeps everything else byte-identical. That delta form is the cleanest available template for NT-3 and is not cited.
findings.remedy: Rename the field to canonicalRelationPayloadHex and add decodedRelationPayload, following the live vector.

findings.title: NT-3 anchor names a snapshot path with no pinned snapshot membership
findings.live: fact-plane anchorSchema variant source-span: 'snapshotId/path/contentSha256/startByte/endByte are non-null and match one sealed Snapshot file'. sourceSpanSchema.rule: 'path is a normalized project-relative NFC path in the sealed Snapshot and [startByte,endByte) is a non-empty in-bounds byte interval.' The live vector pins context.snapshotFiles with path, contentSha256 and byteLength so the anchor is checkable.
findings.authored: path 'bin/entry' with startByte 0, endByte 1 and the contentSha256 of docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/dr-103.v2/dummy.onebyte. fixtureLocalPins pins contentSha256 and snapshotId but not path, and the corpus pins no SnapshotManifestV1 and no snapshotFiles array anywhere.
findings.whyItMatters: 'bin/entry' does not come from any TypeScript snapshot; grep places it in the DR-103 component-manifest fixture corpus. As authored the anchor commits to membership in a sealed Snapshot that is never authored, so it cannot be validated either way. The same gap sits under subjectScopeCommitment, which delivery.v2 defines as a commitment over the sorted SnapshotFileSubjectV1 array — the corpus substitutes a fixture-local digest with no member array behind it. Occupancy v2 requires each NT-5 record to retain the host-requested domain, and the domain is defined relative to that subject scope.
findings.remedy: Pin a minimal fixture-local snapshot — one entry, path, contentSha256, byteLength 1 — and derive subjectScopeCommitment from it, or state explicitly that snapshot membership is an unauthored precondition carried into execution.

findings.title: EV-2 and EV-3 are separated only by an under-determined prose baseline
findings.where: authoredCatalog.members[1] and members[3], both at path G23.nt5.coverage-declares-complete.json, digest f5b2df81…
findings.live: occupancy v2 retainedEvidence[2].exactByteIntent: 'The record retains the host-requested domain with unknown, the Coverage payload claiming covered, the host refusal, and proof no unknown-to-covered conversion is admitted. This member is not collapsed into EV-2.'
findings.attackAsWordedIsRefuted: The dispatch attack was that the unknown-to-covered member 'silently uses the narrows payload without a distinct host-requested baseline'. It is not silent — members[3].mutation states 'Same complete CoverageV1 payload as the narrows member' outright — and a distinct baseline is supplied. Reusing one payload against two different domains is in principle a legitimate way to isolate EV-3 from EV-2, since the payload is not what differs.
findings.whyItStillFails: The isolation is only as good as the baseline, and per M3 the baseline is a single prose string. Once the two members share byte-identical payloads, the baseline is the entire distinction between them, so it is the one thing that must be authored to exact bytes and is the one thing that is not. 'declares/syntactic recorded unknown' also encodes the host-side unknown state as English inside a key string rather than as the live coverageState enum value.
findings.remedy: Author the EV-3 baseline as a full one-key requested domain plus an explicit recorded host-side coverageState of 'unknown', so the two members differ by pinned bytes rather than by prose. Resolving M3 resolves this.

findings.title: leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded over-claims closure of OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING
findings.live: leftover-join.v4 obligations[3] holds OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING at leftoverDesign true, scoped to 'hostile-but-well-formed admission corpus (DR-133 NT-3, NT-5)'.
findings.whyItMatters: The scope word is well-formed. Given M1, M4 and M5 the authored bytes do not meet that standard, so recording this corpus would measure the obligation closed against bytes that fail the obligation's own naming. The correct closure claim is contingent on the fixtures being well-formed, not merely on their existing at pinned digests.
findings.notAFindingAbout: I do NOT fault the corpus for filing host relation-registry refusal bytes and the subsequent-session view under execution rather than authoring. Those are observations produced by running the harness, and D-056 clause 5 separates authoring from execution. remainderAfterThisCorpus states that split accurately.
findings.remedy: Resolve M1–M5, or narrow the closure claim to the specific limbs actually satisfied.
